facts.statement: Tiktaalik was described by Daeschler, Shubin, and Jenkins in 2006.
facts.quote: authority: Daeschler, Shubin & Jenkins, 2006

facts.statement: Tiktaalik lived during the Late Devonian period, specifically the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Devonian (Frasnian),

facts.statement: Tiktaalik is a monospecific genus of extinct lobe-finned fish from the late Devonian, approximately 375 million years ago, possessing many tetrapod-like features.
facts.quote: Tiktaalik (; ) is a monospecific genus of extinct sarcopterygian (lobe-finned fish) from the late Devonian Period, about 375 Mya (million years ago), having many features similar to those of tetrapods (four-legged animals).

facts.statement: Tiktaalik specimens are estimated to have ranged in total length from 1.25 to 2.75 meters.
facts.quote: Tiktaalik is estimated to have had a total length of 1.25 – 2.75 m on the basis of various specimens.

facts.statement: The first Tiktaalik fossils were discovered in 2004 on Ellesmere Island in Nunavut, Canada.
facts.quote: The first Tiktaalik fossils were found in 2004 on Ellesmere Island in Nunavut, Canada.

facts.statement: The discovery was made by Edward B. Daeschler, Neil H. Shubin, and Farish A. Jenkins Jr., and published in the April 6, 2006 issue of Nature.
facts.quote: The discovery, made by Edward B. Daeschler of the Academy of Natural Sciences, Neil H. Shubin from the University of Chicago, and Harvard University Professor Farish A. Jenkins Jr., was published in the April 6, 2006 issue of Nature and quickly recognized as a transitional form.

facts.statement: When Tiktaalik existed, Ellesmere Island was part of the continent Laurentia, located near the equator with a warm climate.
facts.quote: At the time of the species' existence, Ellesmere Island was part of the continent Laurentia (modern eastern North America and Greenland), which was centered on the equator and had a warm climate.

facts.statement: The specific name roseae honors an anonymous donor.
facts.quote: The specific name roseae honours an anonymous donor.

facts.statement: The largest known Tiktaalik fossils have an estimated length of 2.75 meters, with lower jaws reaching 31 centimeters.
facts.quote: Tiktaalik was a large fish: the largest known fossils have an estimated length of 2.75 m, with the longest lower jaws reaching a length of 31 cm.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik had a low, flat skull shape more similar to a salamander than to most fish.
facts.quote: The skull of Tiktaalik was low and flat, more similar in shape to that of a salamander than most fish.

facts.statement: Indentations on the skull suggest Tiktaalik may have had primitive lungs in addition to gills.
facts.quote: These notches may have housed spiracles on the top of the head, which suggest the creature had primitive lungs as well as gills.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik is the earliest-known fish to possess a neck, with the pectoral girdle separate from the skull.
facts.quote: This makes Tiktaalik the earliest-known fish to have a neck, with the pectoral (shoulder) girdle separate from the skull.

facts.statement: There are three main hypotheses regarding digit evolution: symmetric development from radials, neomorphic origin as a new structure, or homology to postaxial radials.
facts.quote: In the early 20th century, most paleontologists considered the digits to develop symmetrically from radials at the tip of the fin. Another school of thought, popularized in the 1940s, argued that the hand was neomorphic. In other words, it was an entirely new structure that spontaneously evolved after the distal axials and radials were reduced. A third hypothesis, emphasized by Shubin and Alberch (1986), is that digits are homologous to postaxial radials in particular.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik had a pelvis nearly the same size as its shoulder girdle, similar to tetrapods.
facts.quote: The pelvis was much larger than in other fish, nearly the same size as the shoulder girdle, like tetrapods.

facts.statement: The orientation of Tiktaalik's hip socket was intermediate between the rear-facing sockets of fish and the sideways-facing sockets of tetrapods.
facts.quote: The orientation of the hip socket is halfway between the rear-facing socket of other fish and the sideways-facing socket of tetrapods.

facts.statement: A well-preserved femur from Tiktaalik specimen MCZ 11916 shows broad, well-defined preaxial and postaxial margins.
facts.quote: The Specimen MCZ 11916 from the Museum of Comparative Zoology reveals a well-preserved femur with broad, well defined preaxial and postaxial margins.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik had about 45 pairs of ribs between its skull and hip region, though its vertebrae were not ossified.
facts.quote: Although the vertebrae are not ossified, there are about 45 pairs of ribs between the skull and the hip region.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik likely had strong lungs and a robust ribcage, traits associated with land-living creatures.
facts.quote: Strong lungs (as supported by the plausible presence of a spiracle) may have led to the evolution of a more robust ribcage, a key evolutionary trait of land-living creatures.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik roseae lived approximately 375 million years ago and is the only species in its genus.
facts.quote: Tiktaalik roseae is the only species classified under the genus. Tiktaalik lived approximately 375 million years ago.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik is considered a transitional fossil between fish and tetrapods, comparable to Archaeopteryx's role between reptiles and birds.
facts.quote: Tiktaalik is a transitional fossil; it is to tetrapods what Archaeopteryx is to birds.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik was originally described as a member of Elpistostegalia, a group of tetrapod-like fish.
facts.quote: In its original description, Tiktaalik was described as a member of Elpistostegalia, a name previously used to refer to particularly tetrapod-like fish such as Elpistostege and Panderichthys.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Panderichthys is closer to tetrapods than Tiktaalik or if the similarity is due to convergence, as suggested by a 2008 paper by Boisvert et al.
facts.quote: However, it was questioned in a 2008 paper by Boisvert et al., who noted that Panderichthys, due to its more derived distal forelimb structure, might be closer to tetrapods than Tiktaalik or even that it was convergent with tetrapods.

facts.statement: One hypothesis suggests that similarities between elpistostegalians and tetrapods result from convergent evolution rather than direct ancestry.
facts.quote: Another approach is that elpistostegalian and tetrapod similarities are a case of convergent evolution.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik possessed lobe-finned fish characteristics but had front fins with arm-like skeletal structures including a shoulder, elbow, and wrist similar to crocodiles.
facts.quote: Tiktaalik generally had the characteristics of a lobe-finned fish, but with front fins featuring arm-like skeletal structures more akin to those of a crocodile, including a shoulder, elbow and wrist.

facts.statement: Discoverers suggested that Tiktaalik likely flexed its proto-limbs on stream floors and pulled itself onto shores for brief periods.
facts.quote: The discoverers said that in all likelihood, Tiktaalik flexed its proto-limbs primarily on the floor of streams and may have pulled itself onto the shore for brief periods.

facts.statement: The 2014 discovery of a strongly built pelvic girdle indicated that Tiktaalik could move in shallow water and across mudflats.
facts.quote: In 2014, the discovery of the animal's pelvic girdle was announced; it was strongly built, indicating the animal could have used them for moving in shallow water and across mudflats.

facts.statement: During Tiktaalik's time, flourishing deciduous plants shed leaves into warm, oxygen-poor shallows, attracting small prey that were difficult for larger fish to catch.
facts.quote: At that period, for the first time, deciduous plants were flourishing and annually shedding leaves into the water, attracting small prey into warm oxygen-poor shallows that were difficult for larger fish to swim in.

facts.statement: Its mix of fish and tetrapod characteristics led discoverers to characterize Tiktaalik as an "ichthyotrapod".
facts.quote: Su mezcla de características ícticas y tetrápodas condujo a sus descubridores a caracterizar a Tiktaalik como un "ictiotrápodo".

facts.statement: Tiktaalik lived approximately 375 million years ago.
facts.quote: Vivió hace aproximadamente 375 millones de años.

Jenkins, Jr, fue publicado en la edición del 6 de abril de 2006 de la revista Nature y rápidamente reconocido como un ejemplo clásico de forma transicional.

facts.statement: A 2008 study showed that Tiktaalik was developing structures allowing it to support itself on solid ground and breathe air, a key intermediate step in the transition to terrestrial life.
facts.quote: Tomando una detallada mirada en el esqueleto interno de Tiktaalik roseae, en la edición del 16 de octubre de 2008 de "Nature, los investigadores mostraron como Tiktaalik estaba ganando estructuras que podrían permitirle apoyarse a sí mismo en suelo sólido y respirar aire, un paso intermedio clave en la transformación del cráneo que acompañó el cambio a la vida terrestre de nuestros antecesores distantes.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik had primarily fish characteristics but possessed limb structures resembling a crocodile's arm, including a shoulder, elbow, and wrist.
facts.quote: Tiktaalik tenía principalmente las características de un pez, pero con las extremidades formando estructuras esqueléticas similares a un brazo, parecidas a las del cocodrilo, incluyendo hombro, codo y muñeca.

facts.statement: It had sharp predator teeth and a neck that could move independently of its body, a trait not found in other fish.
facts.quote: Tenía los dientes afilados de un depredador, y su cuello podía moverse independientemente de su cuerpo, lo que no es posible en otros peces.

facts.statement: The animal had a flat skull like modern amphibians, high-set eyes, and a neck and ribs like tetrapods that supported its body and aided lung breathing.
facts.quote: El animal también tenía un cráneo plano como el de los actuales anfibios; los ojos en lo alto de la cabeza; cuello y costillas como las de los tetrápodos, las cuales le servían para soportar el cuerpo y ayudarle a respirar por los pulmones

facts.statement: It had a long snout capable of hunting prey on land and a gill opening that would evolve into an ear in more advanced animals.
facts.quote: un largo hocico capaz de cazar presas sobre tierra; y una abertura branquial que, en animales más evolucionados, se convertiría en oído.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Tiktaalik likely flexed its proto-limbs on the riverbed and could push itself toward the shore for brief periods.
facts.quote: Sus descubridores opinaron que, con toda probabilidad, Tiktaalik flexionaba sus proto-extremidades en el lecho de los ríos principalmente y podría haberse empujado a sí mismo hacia la orilla por breves periodos.

facts.statement: Specimens of this animal reached a length of 1.2 to 2.75 meters.
facts.quote: Estos especímenes alcanzaron un tamaño de 1.2 a 2.75 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The parent group of Tiktaalik is Panderichthyidae.

facts.statement: Tiktaalik belongs to the family Panderichthyidae.
